title: A template bound rejects an argument that does not satisfy the bound

ground_truth.statement: count_all() declares @template T of \Countable and @param T $value. \Countable is a real interface, and the value passed in the fixture - the array [1, 2, 3] - is not an instance of it ([1,2,3] instanceof Countable is false), so the argument does not satisfy the declared bound. The bound-satisfying control, an ArrayObject, does. The function body itself is legal (count() accepts arrays), so only static analysis can catch the breach.

allowed.reason: Same fact under the argument rule: Mago names the unsatisfied constraint and the rejected value. Verified to be the same line and the same root cause as template-constraint-violation, not a second defect.

notes: A green row with a per-tool code split rather than a defect: PHPStan reports argument.type ('expects Countable'), Psalm reports InvalidArgument, and Mago reports template-constraint-violation plus invalid-argument for the same call. The forbidden predicates on line 26 are the asymmetric control - an ArrayObject does implement Countable and must stay silent for all three, so the reports cannot come from the native signature alone. The bound is not a tool-specific annotation in the sense the contract excludes: \Countable is a native interface and the runtime script decides the violation with instanceof. The pattern came from mago/repro/template-bounds/repro.php, which is a different program; the fixture here is clean-room.
